domain_label: Termination & Well-Foundedness for Recursive Plans (Recursive Planning Engine subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is termination and well-foundedness only; the decomposition method itself and contract composition are delegated to sibling KBs
the recursive plan exposes its recursive call sites and recursion-driving arguments to the prover
a model of reachable states / call arguments and the engine's operational semantics is available
exclusions: the hierarchical decomposition method itself (delegated to htn__decomposition)
interface contracts and assume/guarantee contract composition (delegated to a contract-composition KB)
operator implementation internals and runtime scheduling
general program correctness beyond halting (partial-correctness, functional verification)

competency_questions.question: How is a ranking/variant function defined and what well-founded order does it map into?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RANK_FUNCTION defines the variant; WELLFOUND_ORDER selects the order

competency_questions.question: Is the ranking function total and defined on every reachable state?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOTALITY_CHECK establishes totality over the reachable set

competency_questions.question: How are base cases identified and shown to be the minimal elements of the order?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BASE_CASE proves base cases coincide with minimal elements

competency_questions.question: Is the measure sound with respect to the operational semantics of the engine?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEASURE_SOUNDNESS ties the proof rank to the executed rank

competency_questions.question: How is strict, monotone decrease proven on every recursive step?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROGRESS_MEASURE proves strict decrease; MONOTONICITY_CHECK audits monotonicity

competency_questions.question: How are composite (lexicographic/multiset) and mutual-recursion measures built and lifted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEASURE_COMPOSITION composes measures; MUTUAL_RECURSION covers call-graph cycles

competency_questions.question: How is a non-decreasing or oscillating step detected and localized?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MONOTONICITY_CHECK audits decrease; OSCILLATION_DETECT localizes stalls

competency_questions.question: How is a per-call-site termination obligation emitted, guarded, and discharged?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TERMINATION_OBLIGATION emits obligations; GUARD_PLACEMENT enforces decrease at call sites

competency_questions.question: What guards and hard depth bounds backstop the recursion?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GUARD_PLACEMENT and DEPTH_CAP provide guard and fallback bounds

competency_questions.question: How is mutual / indirect recursion handled across the call graph?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MUTUAL_RECURSION builds a measure decreasing around every SCC cycle

competency_questions.question: How does a fuel/step budget bound the session and convert non-termination into a defeater?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEPTH_CAP and FUEL_BUDGET bound depth/steps and raise defeaters

competency_questions.question: How do bounded retry and fixpoint convergence criteria terminate iterative loops?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOUNDED_RETRY bounds attempts; CONVERGENCE_CRITERION stops fixpoint iteration; FUEL_BUDGET backstops

competency_questions.question: How is suspected divergence detected and turned into a handleable defeater?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OSCILLATION_DETECT detects stalls; DIVERGENCE_DEFEATER promotes them to defeaters

competency_questions.question: How are convergence and productivity distinguished from termination for iterative and infinite processes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONVERGENCE_CRITERION and PRODUCTIVITY treat fixpoint and co-recursive cases

glossary.definition: a binary relation with no infinite strictly descending chain, the foundation of every termination argument
a function from states/call-arguments into a well-founded set that strictly decreases on recursive calls
the well-founded order on tuples comparing component-wise left to right, used for multi-argument recursion
the Dershowitz-Manna well-founded order on finite multisets, lifting a base order to bags of elements
a per-call-site proof goal that the variant strictly decreases for that recursive call
a finite step budget decremented per recursive step whose exhaustion forces a defeater
a structured, handleable signal that suspends a recursive plan when divergence is suspected
for co-recursion, the guarantee that each step yields a finite observable prefix in finite time
a machine-checkable bundle of order, rank and per-call-site proofs that re-verifies halting

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for termination and well-foundedness work units, informed by classical termination and well-founded-set theory; no supplied dataset or benchmark
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Turing 1949 'Checking a Large Routine'; Floyd 1967 'Assigning Meanings to Programs' (well-founded sets); Dershowitz & Manna 1979 'Proving Termination with Multiset Orderings'; Bertot & Casteran 2004 'Interactive Theorem Proving and Program Development' (well-founded and guarded recursion); Cousot & Cousot, ranking-function / termination analysis

nodes.definition: Select and justify a well-founded order (a relation with no infinite strictly descending chain) over the codomain the ranking function maps into, e.g. (N,<), ordinals, or a lexicographic/multiset extension.

included: choice of order (N,< / ordinals / lexicographic / multiset)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the chosen order's well-foundedness assumption or codomain changes

pros.claim: A well-founded order is the single hypothesis that turns 'measure decreases' into 'recursion halts' (Floyd's well-founded sets)
pros.example: (N,<) admits no infinite descending chain, so a strictly decreasing N-valued measure must reach a minimum

cons.claim: Picking too weak an order (e.g. (Q>=0,<)) breaks well-foundedness and silently invalidates every downstream proof
cons.example: 0,1/2,1/4,... descends forever in the rationals: a measure into Q>=0 proves nothing

failure_modes: order assumed well-founded but is not (dense or unbounded-below)
conflating a partial order with a well-founded one
acceptance_tests: the selected order is proven or cited to have no infinite descending chain
the codomain of the ranking function is exactly this order's carrier
revisit_triggers: order replaced or generalized to ordinals
a descending chain is exhibited in the chosen order

nodes.definition: Define a ranking (variant) function mapping each reachable state / recursive-call argument tuple into the carrier of the well-founded order, so that recursion behaviour is summarized by a single comparable quantity.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the argument structure or state representation the rank reads from changes

pros.claim: A variant function reduces an open-ended halting question to arithmetic/order comparison on a single value (Turing's quantity that decreases)
pros.example: rank(ackermann m n)=(m,n) collapses the whole recursion to one lexicographic pair

cons.claim: A rank that ignores a recursion-driving argument cannot be made to decrease and will block the proof
cons.example: measuring only list length misses a recursion that shrinks an embedded tree, not the list

failure_modes: rank omits an argument that actually drives recursion
rank is not a function (multi-valued on equal states)
acceptance_tests: the ranking function is total on reachable states and lands in the order's carrier
its value is determined by the recursion-driving arguments
revisit_triggers: recursion-driving arguments change
a recursive call is found that the current rank cannot distinguish

nodes.definition: Identify the recursion's base cases and prove they coincide with the minimal elements of the well-founded order: when the rank is minimal, no further recursive call is issued.

included: proof base case implies no recursive call

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the base-case predicate or minimal elements of the order change

pros.claim: Anchoring base cases at the order's minimum makes induction along the order discharge the whole recursion
pros.example: rank=0 is exactly 'empty input', the terminating leaf

cons.claim: A base case not at the minimum leaves a gap where the rank can still decrease but recursion stops early or never
cons.example: stopping at length<=1 while rank counts pairs leaves an unhandled length-1 case

failure_modes: a reachable minimal-rank state still issues a recursive call
base predicate and minimal element disagree
acceptance_tests: every minimal-rank reachable state is a non-recursing base case
every base case is reachable and handled
revisit_triggers: base-case predicate revised
a recursive call observed at minimal rank

nodes.definition: Establish that the ranking function is total and defined on every reachable state / call argument, so the proof never compares an undefined rank and no reachable call escapes the measure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the reachable-state set or the rank's domain definition changes

pros.claim: Totality on reachable states closes the 'measure undefined here' loophole that makes a decrease proof vacuous
pros.example: every node a recursive call can reach has a defined rank, so the decrease is always checkable

cons.claim: Proving totality over an over-approximated reachable set can demand discharging unreachable, hard cases
cons.example: including dead branches forces a rank for inputs the planner never produces

failure_modes: rank undefined on a reachable argument
reachable set under-approximated, missing a real state
acceptance_tests: the ranking function is defined on every reachable state
unreachable states are excluded with justification
revisit_triggers: reachable-state over/under-approximation revised
an undefined-rank state is reached in a trace

nodes.definition: Show the ranking function and its decrease are sound with respect to the operational semantics: the rank the proof manipulates is the rank the executed recursive call actually carries, with no abstraction gap.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the operational semantics or the state/argument abstraction the rank reads changes

pros.claim: Soundness ties the paper proof to the running engine, so a discharged obligation actually constrains execution
pros.example: the rank is computed from the same arguments the interpreter binds at the call, not a model of them

cons.claim: A faithful semantic model is expensive and an over-idealized one can certify a recursion that diverges in practice
cons.example: modelling integers as unbounded hides an overflow that resets the rank and loops

failure_modes: abstraction gap: proven rank differs from executed rank
unmodeled side effect mutates the recursion-driving argument
acceptance_tests: the rank used in the proof provably equals the rank of the executed call
abstractions are justified or shown sound
revisit_triggers: operational semantics revised
a divergence reproduced that the proof did not predict

nodes.definition: Prove the ranking function strictly decreases, in the well-founded order, on every recursive step: for each call site, rank(callee args) < rank(caller args).

included: the decrease inequality in the order

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a recursive call site is added, removed, or its argument transformation changes

pros.claim: Strict decrease plus well-foundedness is the complete classical termination argument (Floyd/Turing variant method)
pros.example: each recursive call on a strictly smaller sublist guarantees the descent bottoms out

cons.claim: A measure that decreases on some but not all call sites proves nothing; one non-decreasing edge breaks it
cons.example: a fast path that recurses on the same size leaves a non-decreasing step

failure_modes: a call site where the rank does not strictly decrease
non-strict (<=) decrease mistaken for strict (<)
acceptance_tests: every recursive call site exhibits rank(callee) < rank(caller) in the chosen order
the decrease is strict, not merely non-increasing
revisit_triggers: a new recursive call site is introduced
a non-decreasing step is found in a trace

nodes.definition: Compose measures for multi-argument or structurally rich recursion using lexicographic products, multiset orderings (Dershowitz-Manna), or product/ordinal combinations, lifting component well-foundedness to the composite.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the number/structure of recursion-driving arguments changes

pros.claim: Lexicographic and multiset orderings prove terminations no single scalar can, while staying well-founded
pros.example: Ackermann needs lexicographic (m,n); rewrite systems need the multiset order over redexes

cons.claim: Composite measures multiply proof obligations: each component and the lift must be discharged, raising cost sharply
cons.example: a 3-tuple lexicographic measure needs decrease/no-increase reasoning across all three positions per call

failure_modes: wrong component dominates the lexicographic comparison
multiset extension applied to a non-well-founded base
acceptance_tests: the composite order is shown well-founded from its components
each call decreases the composite in the defined sense
revisit_triggers: argument structure changes
a single scalar measure is found to suffice (simplify) or to fail (escalate)

nodes.definition: Verify the claimed decrease is genuinely monotone with respect to the order on every step and across composition: no step increases or holds the rank, and the comparison operator matches the order's direction.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the comparison operator or the order's direction convention changes

pros.claim: An explicit monotonicity audit catches the most common termination bug: a sign or <=/< slip that voids the descent
pros.example: flags a step proven with <= that the proof treated as <

cons.claim: Monotonicity over a coarse abstraction can pass while the concrete step does not strictly decrease
cons.example: abstracting two distinct sizes to one bucket hides a non-decreasing concrete step

failure_modes: off-by-direction comparison (proving increase)
a held-rank step counted as a decrease
acceptance_tests: every recursive step is verified to strictly move down the order
comparison direction matches the order definition
revisit_triggers: order direction convention changes
a non-monotone step is detected

nodes.definition: Emit and discharge one explicit termination proof obligation per recursive call site: a checkable goal of the form 'this call's rank is strictly below the enclosing rank in the order', tracked to closed.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the set of recursive call sites or the obligation schema changes

pros.claim: Per-call-site obligations make termination a finite, enumerable checklist rather than a global hand-wave
pros.example: each of the 4 recursive calls becomes a named, individually discharged lemma

cons.claim: Obligations proliferate with call sites and higher-order calls, and an unlisted indirect call leaves a silent gap
cons.example: a call hidden behind a function-valued parameter never gets an obligation

failure_modes: a recursive call site with no emitted obligation
an obligation marked discharged without a real proof
acceptance_tests: every recursive call site has an emitted obligation
every obligation is discharged or routed to a defeater
revisit_triggers: a call site is added or discovered
an obligation is found discharged without proof

nodes.definition: Place recursion guards / decreasing-checks at each call site that assert the variant strictly decreased before the call proceeds, turning a static obligation into a runtime-enforceable guard.

included: guard at each recursive call site

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the guard insertion policy or call-site instrumentation changes

pros.claim: A decreasing-check guard converts a violated variant from silent divergence into an immediate, localized failure
pros.example: the guard fires the instant a call is issued with a non-smaller rank, naming the offending site

cons.claim: Guards add per-call overhead and a too-loose guard (<= instead of <) admits the very non-termination it should stop
cons.example: a guard checking 'not larger' lets equal-rank loops slip through

failure_modes: guard uses non-strict comparison
a call site instrumented without a guard
acceptance_tests: each recursive call site carries a strict-decrease guard
guard violation raises a handleable defeater
revisit_triggers: guard policy changes
a guard with non-strict comparison is found

nodes.definition: Handle mutual and indirect recursion by a shared or summed/tagged measure that strictly decreases around every cycle in the call graph, not merely within a single function.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the call graph's strongly connected components change

pros.claim: A measure that decreases around each call-graph cycle proves mutual recursion that per-function measures cannot
pros.example: f calls g calls f: a tag-lexicographic measure decreases over the f->g->f cycle

cons.claim: Indirect recursion through higher-order or dynamic dispatch can hide a cycle the SCC analysis never sees
cons.example: a callback re-enters the recursion via a registered handler, invisible to static call-graph extraction

failure_modes: a call-graph cycle with no decreasing shared measure
an indirect/dynamic call edge missing from the graph
acceptance_tests: every strongly connected component of the call graph has a measure that strictly decreases around it
indirect edges are captured
revisit_triggers: call graph topology changes
a hidden indirect recursion cycle is discovered

nodes.definition: Impose a hard maximum recursion/decomposition depth as a fallback bound that guarantees halting even when a variant proof is absent or incomplete, raising a defeater on breach.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the depth-cap value or fallback policy changes

pros.claim: A depth cap is a soundness backstop: it guarantees the engine halts regardless of proof completeness
pros.example: depth>64 halts and reports, so an unproven recursion can never hang the session

cons.claim: A cap tight enough to be safe can truncate a legitimately deep but terminating recursion, hurting completeness
cons.example: a correct 80-level decomposition is cut at a cap of 64 and reported as a false defeater

failure_modes: cap below the true required depth (false defeater)
cap so high it never bounds real blow-up in time
acceptance_tests: recursion depth is bounded by an explicit hard cap
a breach raises a defeater rather than crashing
revisit_triggers: depth-cap policy changes
a valid deep recursion is truncated by the cap

nodes.definition: Allocate a fuel / step budget consumed by each recursive step so that exhaustion converts suspected non-termination into an explicit, catchable defeater rather than an unbounded hang.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the fuel allocation formula or accounting granularity changes

pros.claim: Fuel makes non-termination observable and recoverable: the session is bounded by construction (a step budget that always runs out)
pros.example: budget 10000 steps means the worst case is a defeater after 10000 steps, never a hang

cons.claim: Fuel that is too small cuts off a slow-but-terminating computation early, producing a soundness-irrelevant false defeater
cons.example: a correct computation needing 12000 steps is killed at a 10000-step budget

failure_modes: budget too small (early cutoff of valid runs)
fuel accounting misses steps, so the bound is not real
acceptance_tests: every recursive step consumes fuel and exhaustion raises a defeater
the budget bounds the whole session
revisit_triggers: fuel allocation policy changes
a valid computation is cut off by fuel exhaustion

nodes.definition: Detect non-decreasing cycles and oscillation: recurring states or rank values that never strictly descend, signalling the variant is not actually decreasing on some loop.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the state-equality or rank-fingerprint definition used to detect cycles changes

pros.claim: Catching a repeated rank or state pinpoints exactly where the descent stalls, far more precisely than a bare timeout
pros.example: spotting rank revisiting value 7 twice localizes the non-decreasing loop

cons.claim: State-hashing for cycle detection can false-positive on benign revisits and costs memory proportional to history
cons.example: a memoized re-derivation revisits a state legitimately and is flagged as oscillation

failure_modes: benign revisit flagged as oscillation
a genuine stall missed because state fingerprint is too coarse
acceptance_tests: a non-strictly-decreasing cycle is detected and localized to its call site
stalls are distinguished from progress
revisit_triggers: state-equality definition changes
an oscillation escapes detection until fuel exhaustion

nodes.definition: Define a convergence criterion for fixpoint-style / iterative loops: a threshold or stable-difference test under which the iteration is declared converged and terminates, with the decreasing residual as its variant.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the convergence threshold or residual metric changes

pros.claim: A convergence threshold gives iterative/fixpoint loops a principled stop that a structural variant cannot express
pros.example: a numeric fixpoint stops when successive iterates differ by < epsilon

cons.claim: A threshold set too loose stops short of the true fixpoint; too tight may never be met under floating error and loops
cons.example: epsilon below machine precision makes the residual test never fire

failure_modes: threshold never met (effective non-termination)
premature convergence to a non-fixpoint
acceptance_tests: the iteration terminates when the residual crosses the threshold
the residual provably decreases toward the threshold
revisit_triggers: residual metric or threshold changes
an iteration fails to converge under the threshold

nodes.definition: Replace unbounded retry/iteration loops with an explicitly bounded retry counter so that retry-style recursion (re-attempt on failure) terminates after a fixed number of attempts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the retry-bound policy or backoff schedule changes

pros.claim: A retry counter is a trivially well-founded variant (counts down to zero), making retry loops provably finite
pros.example: at most 5 attempts: the attempt count is a decreasing N-valued variant

cons.claim: A retry bound too low abandons a transiently failing operation that would have succeeded on the next attempt
cons.example: giving up after 3 retries on a service that recovers on the 4th

failure_modes: unbounded retry on a persistent failure
bound so low it abandons recoverable work
acceptance_tests: every retry loop has an explicit decreasing attempt bound
exhaustion raises a defeater not a hang
revisit_triggers: retry-bound policy changes
a recoverable operation is abandoned by a too-low bound

nodes.definition: Treat suspected divergence (variant stall, oscillation, or budget exhaustion) as a first-class, handleable defeater that suspends the recursive plan and routes to repair, rather than an uncatchable hang.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the divergence-signal taxonomy or defeater routing changes

pros.claim: Promoting divergence to a defeater makes non-termination a recoverable planning event instead of a fatal hang
pros.example: a stall signal suspends the subplan and hands a defeater to the planner's repair loop

cons.claim: A defeater raised on weak evidence (one slow step) aborts computations that would have terminated, trading completeness for safety
cons.example: a single expensive step trips the defeater and discards a converging run

failure_modes: divergence defeater raised on a converging computation
real divergence not aggregated into a defeater
acceptance_tests: suspected divergence raises a structured defeater that suspends the plan
the defeater carries the offending site and signal
revisit_triggers: divergence taxonomy changes
a divergence escaped as an uncatchable hang

nodes.definition: For co-recursive / streaming processes that are not meant to terminate, prove productivity (guardedness): each step yields a finite observable prefix in finite time, the dual of termination for infinite output.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the stream/codata semantics or guardedness criterion changes

pros.claim: Productivity certifies useful non-terminating processes (streams, servers) that termination would wrongly reject (Bertot-Casteran guarded corecursion)
pros.example: a guarded stream definition yields one element per step, productive though infinite

cons.claim: Productivity and termination pull opposite ways: forcing a termination measure on a stream rejects a correct process
cons.example: demanding a decreasing variant on an event loop wrongly flags a productive server as non-terminating

failure_modes: unguarded corecursion (no observable prefix per step)
termination criterion misapplied to a co-recursive process
acceptance_tests: each co-recursive step is proven to emit a finite prefix in finite time
productive processes are not failed by termination checks
revisit_triggers: codata semantics change
a process is found unproductive (stalls without output)

nodes.definition: When termination cannot be proven, construct an explicit witness/counterexample of non-termination: an infinite descending-free run, a recurrent state, or a non-decreasing cycle, as evidence the recursion truly diverges.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the witness schema or what counts as a divergence proof changes

pros.claim: A concrete non-termination witness turns a failed proof into actionable evidence: it shows the actual diverging run
pros.example: a lasso (stem + repeated cycle with no rank decrease) demonstrates the loop is truly infinite

cons.claim: Constructing a sound witness is itself hard, and a spurious witness from an over-approximation falsely condemns a terminating recursion
cons.example: an abstract cycle that no concrete run realizes wrongly labels the recursion non-terminating

failure_modes: spurious witness from an over-approximate model
no witness found yet termination still unproven (inconclusive)
acceptance_tests: a constructed witness is checked to be a genuine non-terminating run
spurious abstract witnesses are refuted
revisit_triggers: witness schema changes
a witness is found to be spurious under concrete semantics

nodes.definition: Assemble a machine-checkable termination certificate: the chosen order, ranking function, per-call-site decrease proofs, base cases, mutual-recursion coverage, and fallback bounds, bundled so an external checker can re-verify halting.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the certificate schema or the external checker's interface changes

pros.claim: A self-contained certificate lets a cheap external checker re-verify termination without trusting the prover (proof-carrying termination)
pros.example: the certificate replays each call-site decrease so a small kernel re-checks the whole proof

cons.claim: A certificate that omits a call site or the well-foundedness witness is unsound yet looks complete; assembly is the last place gaps hide
cons.example: a certificate missing the mutual-recursion SCC coverage certifies a recursion that can still loop

failure_modes: certificate missing a call site or the order's well-foundedness witness
certificate not independently re-checkable
acceptance_tests: the certificate bundles order, rank, every discharged obligation, base cases and fallbacks
an external checker re-verifies it independently
revisit_triggers: certificate schema changes
an external re-check of the certificate fails

edges.why_related: both are fallback session bounds; fuel is step-based, depth-cap is depth-based
an undischargeable obligation feeds back as a divergence defeater
a detected non-decreasing cycle refutes the claimed strict-decrease measure
the decrease proof is only valid where the measure is total
guards must be placed around every call-graph cycle, not just direct self-calls
both terminate iterative loops: one by attempt count, one by residual threshold
a missing/mis-placed base case is a common root cause a non-termination witness exposes
a tight depth cap guarantees halting but can truncate a terminating-yet-deep recursion, undermining the completeness the certificate aims to establish
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the termination argument
edges.resolution_rule: prefer a proven variant over the depth cap: the cap is a soundness backstop, not a substitute for the certificate; raise the cap only when the certificate shows the truncated depth is genuinely required and reachable

edges.why_related: a small fuel budget can cut off a sound, terminating computation early, so fuel exhaustion is not by itself a sound non-termination conclusion
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the termination argument
edges.resolution_rule: size fuel above the soundly-proven worst-case bound when a variant exists, so exhaustion can only mean genuine divergence; use a small fuel only as a last-resort cutoff and label exhaustion as inconclusive, not as proof of non-termination

edges.why_related: richer lexicographic/multiset measures discharge more obligations but multiply the per-call-site proof cost, trading expressiveness against proof effort
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the termination argument
edges.resolution_rule: use the least expressive measure that discharges all obligations: try a scalar variant first; escalate to lexicographic then multiset only when an obligation cannot be discharged, accepting the higher proof cost only where needed

edges.why_related: termination via a decreasing measure and productivity for infinite output are dual and mutually exclusive goals; applying the wrong one rejects a correct process
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the termination argument
edges.resolution_rule: classify the process first: require a strictly decreasing variant (PROGRESS_MEASURE) for processes that must terminate, and require guardedness/productivity instead for intentionally infinite co-recursive processes; never impose a termination measure on a productive stream

conflict_axes.name: depth_cap_tightness_vs_completeness
conflict_axes.description: A tight hard depth cap guarantees halting but can truncate a legitimately deep terminating recursion; a loose cap risks long blow-up before tripping.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the cap as a backstop; raise it only against a proven, reachable required depth

conflict_axes.name: fuel_soundness_vs_early_cutoff
conflict_axes.description: Fuel converts non-termination into a defeater, but a small budget cuts off slow-yet-terminating runs and a large one delays the defeater.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: size fuel above the proven worst case where a variant exists; label exhaustion inconclusive otherwise

conflict_axes.name: measure_expressiveness_vs_proof_cost
conflict_axes.description: Lexicographic/multiset measures prove more terminations than scalars but multiply per-call-site proof obligations.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the least expressive measure that discharges all obligations; escalate only on failure

conflict_axes.name: termination_vs_productivity
conflict_axes.description: Finite recursion needs a decreasing variant; infinite co-recursion needs productivity instead. The two criteria are dual and exclusive.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: classify the process first; apply the matching criterion, never both

conflict_axes.name: static_proof_vs_runtime_guard
conflict_axes.description: A static variant proof gives certainty before running but costs proof effort; runtime decreasing-check guards are cheap to add but only fail at run time.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prove statically where feasible; keep guards as a runtime backstop and defeater source

conflict_axes.name: reachable_set_over_vs_under_approximation
conflict_axes.description: Over-approximating reachable states forces proving hard unreachable cases; under-approximating leaves a real state with an undefined or undecreased rank.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: approximate tightly with justification; recheck on reachable-set changes

conflict_axes.name: convergence_threshold_loose_vs_tight
conflict_axes.description: A loose fixpoint convergence threshold stops short of the true fixpoint; a tight one may never be met under numerical error and effectively loops.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set the threshold from the residual metric's known precision; back it with fuel

conflict_axes.name: eager_defeater_vs_completeness
conflict_axes.description: Raising a divergence defeater on weak evidence aborts computations that would have terminated; waiting for strong evidence risks longer hangs.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require a corroborated signal (oscillation plus budget pressure) before defeating

conflict_axes.name: witness_soundness_vs_construction_cost
conflict_axes.description: A concrete non-termination witness is strong evidence but expensive to build soundly; an abstract one is cheap but can be spurious.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: build abstract first to localize, then concretize before condemning the recursion

edge_cases.description: A recursive call passes the same argument, so the variant does not strictly decrease and the recursion runs forever.
edge_cases.trigger: a call site recurses with rank(callee) = rank(caller)
edge_cases.mitigation: require strict (<) decrease per call site; a held-rank step is a discharge failure

edge_cases.description: The ranking function maps into a dense or unbounded-below order, so 'decreasing' admits an infinite chain and proves nothing.
edge_cases.trigger: codomain is (Q>=0,<) or similar non-well-founded order
edge_cases.mitigation: map into a proven well-founded order (N, ordinals, lexicographic/multiset)

edge_cases.description: A reachable state has no defined rank, so the decrease proof is vacuous exactly where it is needed.
edge_cases.trigger: rank is partial and undefined on a reachable argument
edge_cases.mitigation: prove totality over the reachable set or exclude unreachable states with justification

edge_cases.description: Mutual recursion through f->g->f decreases within neither function alone, so per-function measures miss the divergence.
edge_cases.trigger: a call-graph cycle with no shared decreasing measure
edge_cases.mitigation: build a shared/tagged measure that decreases around every SCC of the call graph

edge_cases.description: Indirect recursion via a higher-order callback re-enters the recursion through an edge the static call graph never recorded.
edge_cases.trigger: a dynamic/higher-order call edge missing from the analyzed graph
edge_cases.mitigation: capture indirect edges; guard at runtime where static capture is impossible

edge_cases.description: A hard depth cap truncates a correct but deep decomposition, reporting a false non-termination defeater.
edge_cases.trigger: depth cap set below the true required depth
edge_cases.mitigation: raise the cap only when the certificate proves the depth is required and reachable

edge_cases.description: A small fuel budget kills a slow-but-terminating computation, and exhaustion is misread as proof of non-termination.
edge_cases.trigger: fuel below the proven worst-case step count
edge_cases.mitigation: size fuel above the worst case where a variant exists; label bare exhaustion inconclusive

edge_cases.description: A fixpoint iteration's convergence threshold is below machine precision, so the residual test never fires and the loop runs until fuel exhaustion.
edge_cases.trigger: convergence epsilon smaller than the residual metric's precision
edge_cases.mitigation: derive the threshold from the metric's known precision; backstop with fuel

edge_cases.description: A productive infinite process (event loop / stream) is wrongly failed because a termination measure was demanded of it.
edge_cases.trigger: a co-recursive process subjected to a decreasing-variant check
edge_cases.mitigation: classify as co-recursive and require guardedness/productivity, not termination

edge_cases.description: A non-termination witness is built from an over-approximate model and condemns a recursion that actually terminates.
edge_cases.trigger: an abstract cycle with no concrete realizing run is accepted as a witness
edge_cases.mitigation: concretize the abstract witness before condemning; refute spurious ones

edge_cases.description: The abstraction the proof reasons over diverges from the executed semantics, so a discharged obligation does not actually constrain the run.
edge_cases.trigger: the proof rank differs from the rank the interpreter computes at the call
edge_cases.mitigation: prove the proof rank equals the executed rank; justify every abstraction

edge_cases.description: The assembled certificate omits one recursive call site, so it certifies a recursion that can still loop through the missing site.
edge_cases.trigger: a call site has no obligation in the certificate bundle
edge_cases.mitigation: enumerate all call sites (including indirect) before sealing the certificate

workflow.description: Choose and justify a well-founded order (N, ordinals, lexicographic, or multiset) with no infinite descending chain.
workflow.gate: the order is proven or cited to have no infinite descent

workflow.description: Define the variant function from reachable states/arguments into the order's carrier.
workflow.gate: rank reads the recursion-driving arguments and lands in the carrier

workflow.description: Prove the rank is total on every reachable state; exclude unreachable states with justification.
workflow.gate: no reachable state has an undefined rank

workflow.description: Show base cases coincide with the order's minimal elements and issue no recursive call.
workflow.gate: every minimal-rank reachable state is a non-recursing base case

workflow.description: Prove rank(callee) < rank(caller) strictly, in the order, at every recursive call site.
workflow.gate: every call site exhibits strict decrease

workflow.description: Compose lexicographic/multiset measures and ensure decrease around every call-graph cycle.
workflow.gate: every SCC has a decreasing shared measure

workflow.description: Audit that each step strictly moves down the order with the correct comparison direction.
workflow.gate: no non-decreasing or wrong-direction step remains

workflow.description: Emit one obligation per call site and place strict-decrease guards at each.
workflow.gate: every call site has an emitted, discharged-or-routed obligation

workflow.description: Install the depth cap and fuel budget as backstops that raise defeaters on breach.
workflow.gate: depth and step bounds are configured and breach-defeating

workflow.description: Detect non-decreasing cycles/oscillation and aggregate signals for the defeater.
workflow.gate: stalls are detected and localized to a call site

workflow.description: Raise a divergence defeater on corroborated signals; construct a witness when proof fails.
workflow.gate: divergence is a handleable defeater, not a hang

workflow.description: Bundle order, rank, per-call-site proofs, base cases, mutual coverage and fallbacks into a re-checkable certificate.
workflow.gate: an external checker re-verifies the certificate

priority_rationale: WELLFOUND_ORDER and RANK_FUNCTION are foundational; TOTALITY_CHECK, BASE_CASE and MEASURE_SOUNDNESS underwrite the core PROGRESS_MEASURE and its composition; obligations, guards and mutual-recursion coverage discharge per call site; depth/fuel bounds, oscillation detection and the divergence defeater backstop the session; the machine-checkable TERMINATION_CERTIFICATE seals the proof last.

dominance_rules.rule: WELLFOUND_ORDER must be proven well-founded before any decrease proof is accepted
dominance_rules.rationale: a decrease in a non-well-founded order proves nothing
dominance_rules.trigger: a decrease lemma is accepted against an unjustified order
dominance_rules.action: block acceptance until the order's no-infinite-descent is proven or cited

dominance_rules.rule: PROGRESS_MEASURE must show strict (<) decrease at every call site, not <=
dominance_rules.rationale: a single non-strict or non-decreasing call site voids the whole argument
dominance_rules.trigger: a call site proven with non-strict decrease
dominance_rules.action: reject and require a strictly decreasing measure or a defeater

dominance_rules.rule: TOTALITY_CHECK must pass before PROGRESS_MEASURE is certified
dominance_rules.rationale: a decrease proof is vacuous where the rank is undefined
dominance_rules.trigger: strict-decrease claimed on a partial rank
dominance_rules.action: require totality on the reachable set first

dominance_rules.rule: MUTUAL_RECURSION coverage must decrease around every call-graph SCC before the certificate seals
dominance_rules.trigger: an SCC with no shared decreasing measure
dominance_rules.action: require a shared/tagged measure per SCC

dominance_rules.rule: A proven variant dominates the DEPTH_CAP and FUEL_BUDGET fallbacks for the completeness verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: fallbacks bound the session but a tight bound can falsely truncate a terminating run
dominance_rules.trigger: a fallback breach reported as non-termination while a variant exists
dominance_rules.action: treat the breach as inconclusive when a sound variant is present

dominance_rules.rule: PRODUCTIVITY, not a termination measure, governs intentionally infinite co-recursive processes
dominance_rules.rationale: termination and productivity are dual; the wrong one rejects a correct process
dominance_rules.trigger: a decreasing-variant check applied to a co-recursive process

dominance_rules.rule: FUEL_BUDGET exhaustion alone is not a sound proof of non-termination
dominance_rules.rationale: a small budget can cut off a slow terminating run
dominance_rules.action: label exhaustion inconclusive and require a witness or larger budget

dominance_rules.rule: DIVERGENCE_DEFEATER requires a corroborated signal before aborting a running computation
dominance_rules.rationale: defeating on weak evidence kills computations that would terminate
dominance_rules.trigger: a defeater raised on a single slow step
dominance_rules.action: require oscillation plus budget pressure (or a witness) before defeating

dominance_rules.rule: TERMINATION_CERTIFICATE must enumerate every call site, including indirect ones, before sealing
dominance_rules.rationale: one missing site certifies a recursion that can still loop
dominance_rules.trigger: a call site absent from the obligation ledger
dominance_rules.action: block sealing until all sites (direct and indirect) are covered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not write decrease proofs before fixing the well-founded order; changing the order invalidates every decrease lemma
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-proving all per-call-site decreases after a late order change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not define the ranking function before identifying all recursion-driving arguments; a rank missing one must be redefined
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redefining the variant and redoing every decrease proof

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not certify decrease before totality; a partial rank discovered late forces re-checking every step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-auditing all decrease lemmas after a totality gap surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not size the fuel budget below the proven worst case; raising it after false defeaters re-runs the analysis
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-tuning fuel and re-running runs killed by a too-small budget

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not set the depth cap without certificate feedback; a too-tight cap surfaces as false defeaters late
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-planning after a valid deep recursion is truncated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not impose a termination measure on a co-recursive process; reclassifying after the fact discards the measure work
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discarding a termination measure built for a process that needed productivity

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip mutual-recursion SCC coverage; discovering an uncovered cycle late forces a measure redesign
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesigning the measure after an indirect-recursion divergence is found

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not seal the certificate with an incomplete call-site enumeration; a missing site forces re-opening and re-checking
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-opening a sealed certificate to add a missed call site

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not accept an abstract non-termination witness without concretization; a spurious witness wrongly condemns and triggers needless redesign
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesigning a recursion that actually terminated

iteration_protocol.trigger: a recursive step is found that does not strictly decrease the rank
iteration_protocol.action: strengthen the measure in RANK_FUNCTION/PROGRESS_MEASURE or escalate MEASURE_COMPOSITION to a lexicographic/multiset order

iteration_protocol.trigger: the chosen order is shown not to be well-founded
iteration_protocol.action: reselect a well-founded order in WELLFOUND_ORDER and re-base BASE_CASE on its minimal elements

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reachable state with an undefined rank is observed
iteration_protocol.action: extend totality in TOTALITY_CHECK and re-verify the decrease where it was vacuous

iteration_protocol.trigger: a mutual/indirect recursion cycle escapes the per-function measures
iteration_protocol.action: recompute call-graph SCCs and build a shared measure in MUTUAL_RECURSION

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fallback bound trips on a computation that actually terminates
iteration_protocol.action: raise the bound in DEPTH_CAP/FUEL_BUDGET only against a proven required depth/step count

iteration_protocol.trigger: oscillation is detected without budget exhaustion
iteration_protocol.action: corroborate in OSCILLATION_DETECT and raise a structured defeater via DIVERGENCE_DEFEATER

iteration_protocol.trigger: a non-termination witness is suspected spurious
iteration_protocol.action: concretize and re-check the witness in NONTERM_WITNESS against the operational semantics

iteration_protocol.trigger: an external re-check of the certificate fails
iteration_protocol.action: reopen TERMINATION_CERTIFICATE, find the missing/weak obligation, and re-discharge it

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
